title: Directory Reset for Entire Team
description: The Active Directory directory has become corrupted and is preventing all users from logging in. This is affecting the entire team and site.
resolution:
1. Open Active Directory Users and Computers
2. Select the domain controller that hosts the directory
3. Right-click on the domain name and select Properties
4. Click on the Trusts tab
5. Check the box next to 'Allow logon locally using user account credentials' and click OK
6. Close Active Directory Users and Computers
7. Run the following command: netsh dsreset now
8. Wait for the reset process to complete
9. Test all users' ability to log in.

title: Intermittent Permission Denied Error when accessing Active Directory
description: Users have reported an intermittent issue where they are unable to access Active Directory. The error message displayed is 'Permission denied'. This issue appears to come and go randomly.
resolution:
To resolve this issue, please follow these steps: 
1. Open the Active Directory Users and Computers console.
2. Expand the domain tree by clicking on the triangle next to the domain name in the left-hand pane.
3. Right-click on the OU (Organizational Unit) that is giving permission issues, then select Properties.
4. In the Permissions tab, click on the Advanced button.
5. In the Group Policy Editor, navigate to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Active Directory Users and Computers > Group Policy Object Settings.
6. Double-click on Remove all default permissions from Inherited Group Policy Objects, then select Apply and OK.
7. Close all open applications, then restart the computer. After the restart, log in to Active Directory again and try accessing the OU that was giving permission issues.

A monitoring alert has been fired indicating degraded performance of the API endpoint. An exception was thrown with error message 'API not found'. The payload is as follows:

{"error": "API not found"}
resolution:
1. Check logs for any recent changes or updates to the API. 
2. Validate API documentation and ensure all endpoints are correctly defined. 
3. Review codebase for any dependencies that may have changed or updated. 
4. Check network connectivity between servers hosting the API and client applications. 
5. Test API performance using load testing tools to identify potential bottlenecks or resource constraints.

title: Application domain issue affecting single user
description: User reports that the application is experiencing flapping and stalling issues. The user was attempting to complete a task but was thrown an error message. Upon further investigation, it was discovered that the task had been rolled back. Please investigate the cause of the flapping and stalling issues and resolve the rollback issue.
resolution: The application domain team will investigate the root cause of the flapping and stalling issues by reviewing logs and system performance data. If necessary, the team may perform a system upgrade or patch to address any underlying issues. Once the flapping and stalling issues have been resolved, the team will investigate the rollback issue and take appropriate steps to prevent it from occurring in the future.

title: Payload Error with Application XYZ - Single User
description: The user reports that they are experiencing an error while interacting with the application, resulting in a degraded experience. The issue is occurring consistently and appears to be related to the payload of certain actions. Upon further investigation, it has been determined that there may be issues with the rollback functionality of the application.
resolution:
1. Perform a full system restore from backup to a known stable state.
2. Review the codebase for any potential issues related to payload processing and rollback functionality.
3. Implement fixes as necessary to address any identified issues.
4. Test the application thoroughly to ensure that it is functioning properly after the restoration.

title: Application Incident: Monitoring Alert Fired Overnight
description: We received a monitoring alert that a degraded application was detected overnight. A rollback of the latest update has been initiated to restore the application to its previous stable state.
resolution: 1. The latest update that caused the degradation will be rolled back. This should resolve the issue with the application. 2. Once the rollback is complete, a new update will be released to fix any underlying issues. 3. The system will be monitored for any further incidents.

title: Application API Unresponsive

resolution: Investigate the issue and implement proper validation on the API endpoint to ensure that incoming payloads are properly formatted. Additionally, add error handling to return appropriate status codes for malformed requests.

title: Application domain: Single User Rest Call Exception
description: A single user is encountering an exception when making a REST call to the application. The error message displayed is 'Internal Server Error'. The affected user is unable to proceed with their task and is requesting assistance.

3. Restart the kubectl service on the affected node(s) using the command: "sudo systemctl restart kubelet". This will apply any changes made to the kubelet configuration file.
4. Verify that the pods restarted unexpectedly have been successfully restarted by checking their status using the kubectl get pods command. If any pods continue to fail, please provide additional information or create a separate incident report.

description:

resolution:
Yes, we can definitely help you with that. Please follow these steps to fix the issue:

3. Check your network bandwidth usage: If you are experiencing slow internet speeds, it could be because other users on your network are consuming too much bandwidth. You can check your bandwidth usage by going to Task Manager in Windows and selecting Network. Look for any processes that are using a lot of bandwidth and try to limit their usage if possible.

4. Contact your internet service provider: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, you may need to contact your internet service provider to see if there is an outage or other technical issues affecting your network. They may be able to provide additional assistance or troubleshooting steps.

ipconfig /renewallogicaladdress

Immediate action should be taken to secure the affected systems and prevent further unauthorized access. The following steps should be followed: 
1. Change all affected passwords immediately.
2. Implement two-factor authentication on all affected accounts.
3. Conduct a thorough review of security policies and procedures to identify any vulnerabilities that may have been exploited.
4. Increase user education on safe password practices and the importance of not sharing credentials.

title: Ransomware attack on user account
description: The end-user has reported that they are unable to log into their account due to a ransomware attack. They have received an email asking for payment in exchange for the decryption key.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Change the user's password immediately to prevent further access to their account. 
2. Disconnect any devices that may be infected with malware. 
3. Run a full system scan on all affected devices using a reputable anti-malware software. 
4. Contact your IT department for assistance in decrypting the user's files and restoring access to their account. 
5. Implement stronger security measures, such as multi-factor authentication and regular backups, to prevent future attacks.

title: Incident Report: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive Information
description: A user reported that they were able to access sensitive information through a compromised credential after a recent software update. The user believes the malware may have stolen their password and used it to gain unauthorized access.
resolution: ['Update password policy to require stronger passwords and periodic password changes.', 'Implement multi-factor authentication on all accounts with sensitive data access.', 'Perform a full system scan for malware and other security threats.', 'Conduct an investigation to determine the source of the credentials theft and take appropriate actions.']

title: Complete Failure of IT System Due to Malware Attack and Ransomware Demand
description: The company's IT system has experienced a sudden complete failure, resulting in the loss of critical data and access to essential resources. This incident is believed to have been caused by a malware attack followed by a ransomware demand.
resolution:
1. Remove all infected devices from the network immediately.
2. Perform a full system scan for any remaining malware or viruses.
3. Implement updated security measures, such as firewalls and antivirus software, to prevent future attacks.
4. Restore data from backups if possible.
5. Negotiate with the attackers to release any encrypted files.
6. Update employee training on cybersecurity best practices.

title: Phishing Attempt with Malware Intrusion
description: The user has reported experiencing intermittent phishing attempts and intrusions on their computer. Upon further investigation, malware was detected.
resolution: Please follow these steps to address the issue: 1. Run a full system scan using your antivirus software to remove any existing malware. 2. Update all software, including antivirus software, to the latest version. 3. Enable two-factor authentication on all accounts that were targeted by phishing attempts. 4. Train employees on phishing awareness and provide regular security training for all staff.

title: Storage issue with full disk and mount error
description: The /dev/sda1 disk has reached 100% capacity and cannot be mounted due to an inode limit. The error message displayed in the logs is: 'Error mounting /dev/sda1: Mount failed: Invalid argument'
resolution:
To resolve this issue, please follow these steps: 

1. Free up disk space on the /dev/sda1 disk by deleting unnecessary files or folders. 

2. Run the following command to clear the inode cache: sudo fsck -f /dev/sda1 

3. Mount the disk again using the following command: sudo mount /dev/sda1 /mnt/data

title: Storage Mount Point Error
description: User reports an error when trying to access a disk mounted at /mnt/disk1.
resolution: Check the mount point and ensure that the mount command is correctly specified. If the problem persists, check the file system and run fsck on the disk.

title: Nas Mount Issue
description: User is experiencing issues with their nas mount. Lun appears to be degraded and unable to mount properly.
resolution: 1. Check the status of the lun using the command 'lunstat -l'. If the lun is degraded, run the command 'vgrep' to find the volume group name of the lun. 2. Once you have identified the volume group name, run the command 'VGEDIT [volume group name]' to open the volume group editor. 3. In the editor, click on the 'Resizable Logical Volume (LUN)' tab and select the lun that is experiencing issues. 4. Click the 'Reconfigure' button and follow the prompts to reconfigure the lun. 5. Once the lun has been reconfigured, run the command 'lunstat -l' again to confirm that the lun is no longer degraded. 6. Mount the nas using the appropriate credentials and try accessing the affected file or folder again.

title: Unstable Storage Mount
description: The storage system mounted on team A's servers has been experiencing unstable performance for the past few days, affecting all team members. When attempting to access files or folders, the mount point frequently becomes inaccessible.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Check if there are any pending updates for the storage system software. If yes, install them. 
2. Run a disk check on the mounted volume using the appropriate tool. 
3. Verify that there is enough free space on the volume by checking the disk usage report. 
4. If none of the above steps work, consider replacing the hard drive or upgrading the storage system.

title: Storage flapping incident at point XYZ
description: Storage flapping incident occurred right after update on disk ABC. Disk has been reporting full status since update and causing issues with data access and operations.
resolution: Check disk logs for any error messages related to full status. If logs indicate that a file system repair is needed, initiate a full system scan to repair any damaged files. Once the file system is repaired, check the disk space usage and free up any unnecessary space. Re-run the disk check to ensure the issue has been resolved.

title: Storage device is unstable and causing data loss
description: The storage device (LUN) is experiencing issues and is unable to read or write data correctly. This has resulted in data loss and corruption. The log snippet provided below indicates the issue: Error Code: -127, Inode: <insert inode number>
resolution:
To resolve this issue, follow these steps: 
1. Stop all processes that are using the affected LUN. 
2. Run a full disk scan to repair any damaged or corrupted files. 
3. Verify the integrity of the LUN by checking for any inconsistencies in the file system. If necessary, create a new LUN with a fresh file system. 
4. Once the LUN is stable, you can restart the affected processes and attempt to recover any lost data. Repeat steps as necessary until the issue is resolved.

title: Unstable NAS mount causing delayed file transfers
description: An alert was triggered overnight indicating that a point on the NAS (Network Attached Storage) was becoming unstable. As a result, file transfers from this point have been delayed. Users are reporting that they are unable to access files stored on the affected point.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue:
  • Verify that the network connection is stable.
  • Check if there are any updates available for the NAS software or drivers.
  • Restart the NAS device.
  • Run a disk check on the affected point.
  • If the problem persists, consider replacing the affected point with a new one.

title: Storage Array Flapping and Volume Capacity Issues
description: The end-user has reported that they are unable to access their files on the storage array due to flapping issues and low volume capacity. They are experiencing slow performance and intermittent unavailability of their data.
resolution: 1. Check for any network connectivity issues and verify that the storage array is properly connected to the network. 2. Verify the current volume capacity usage and compare it to the total capacity available on the array. If there is a significant difference, consider expanding the array or consolidating data. 3. Monitor the storage array for any signs of flapping or other performance issues and check the logs for any potential causes. 4. If necessary, perform maintenance or upgrades to improve performance and reliability.

title: Storage Volume Unstable
description: The storage volume for the application server array is gradually becoming unstable over the past few days. This has resulted in slow performance and intermittent errors. The issue is caused by a gradual degradation in the volume capacity.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue:
1. Check if any processes or applications are using up too much of the available storage space. If necessary, optimize the disk usage or add more storage space.
2. Check if there are any issues with the array's configuration, such as incorrectly configured volumes or missing drivers. Ensure that all components are up to date and correctly configured.
3. Run a check on the array for any hardware errors or issues with the storage controller. If there are any issues, replace the faulty component or seek support from the manufacturer.

title: Storage Array Degradation
description: The company's storage array has been experiencing gradual degradation over the past few days, resulting in slow access times and intermittent errors.
resolution:
In order to resolve this issue, the following steps should be taken: 
1. Check the mount point of the affected file system to ensure it is properly mounted. 
2. Verify that the RAID array is functioning correctly by checking the integrity of the parity information. 
3. Review the inode count of the affected directory to identify any issues with individual files or folders. 
4. If necessary, perform a full system scan to detect and repair any corrupted data. 
5. Once all issues have been identified and resolved, run disk checks to ensure that the storage array is functioning properly.

title: Storage Issue: Intermittent Disk Full and Volume Capacity Delays
description: A user has reported an issue with their disk becoming full and delayed volume capacity on a server. The problem is intermittent and comes and goes. The user reports that the disk usage is high and that the system becomes slow to respond.
resolution: 1. Check the disk usage to determine if it is consistently at or near full capacity. 2. If necessary, free up space on the disk by deleting unnecessary files or archiving data. 3. Check for any updates or patches that may be available to improve performance and reduce disk usage. 4. Verify that the volume capacity settings are configured correctly and that there are no issues with the RAID configuration. 5. If the issue persists, contact storage system vendor support for further assistance.

title: Storage issue with flapping mount point
description: The storage volume mounted at /mnt/storage has been flapping and is currently in a degraded state. This has resulted in slow performance and errors when accessing files on the disk.
resolution: ['Check the system logs for any error messages related to the mount point or disk.', 'Verify that the storage volume is properly configured and mounted.', 'Run fsck on the disk to repair any file system issues.', 'If fsck reports errors, run photorep to check for bad sectors and attempt to recover lost data.']

title: Storage RAID Volume Capacity and Inode Issues
description: The storage RAID volume for server XYZ has been experiencing recurring problems where the mount point becomes unavailable, leading to data loss and corruption. The issue appears to be related to the volume capacity and inode issues within the RAID array. The exact cause of the problem is yet to be determined.
resolution:
Please perform the following steps to address this issue: 

1. Log in to the server where the storage RAID volume is mounted using SSH or the local console.
2. Check the status of the volume and ensure that it is available for use. If not, check if any errors are present in the system logs.
3. Run a disk check on the RAID array to verify the integrity of the data stored on the drive. This can be done using the command 'badblocks -v /dev/sda1'. Replace '/dev/sda1' with the appropriate block device name for your RAID array.
4. If any bad blocks are found, run a repair command on the RAID array to fix them. This can be done using the command 'badblocks -v /dev/sda1 | sudo dd if=2>/dev/null bs=65536 count=<number-of-bad-blocks>'. Replace '<number-of-bad-blocks>' with the actual number of bad blocks found during the disk check. 
5. Check the inode usage on the volume using the command 'df -i'. This will show the total number of inodes used on the volume and their usage percentage. If any inodes are at full capacity or beyond, it may be necessary to delete some files or reduce the size of the volume. 
6. Finally, if none of the above steps resolve the issue, please contact storage support for further assistance.

title: Storage issue with gradual degradation
description: The storage system is experiencing a gradual degradation in performance over the past few days. Users have reported that volumes are flapping and becoming unavailable intermittently.
resolution: 1. Check the RAID configuration to ensure it is set up correctly. 2. Verify the volume capacity of all disks to ensure they are not reaching their limits. 3. Perform a disk check on each volume to identify any errors or corruption. 4. Replace any faulty disks if identified. 5. Reboot the storage system and perform a full volume scan.

title: NAS Mount Issue
description: The NAS mount on all systems in the company's Storage domain is causing an issue that affects the entire team and site.
resolution:
1. Reboot all servers involved
2. Check for any updates or patches needed for the NAS software
3. If necessary, reconfigure the RAID array to optimize performance
4. Mount the NAS again and test connectivity
5. Monitor system logs for any errors or issues that may have caused the mount failure

title: NAS Mount Full on LUN - Recurring Problem
description: The NAS mount on the LUN has been experiencing a recurring problem where it becomes full and is unable to be mounted on a regular basis.
resolution: 1. Verify that the LUN has sufficient free space by checking its capacity and usage statistics. 2. Check if there are any pending writes or deletes on the NAS that are causing the mount to become full. If so, wait for them to complete or manually clear them using appropriate commands. 3. Mount the NAS drive again on a different LUN or increase the size of the current LUN if necessary.

title: Storage Degradation - Intermittent Issues with Volume Capacity
description: User reports that the storage volume capacity has been fluctuating and at times becomes degraded, causing issues in storing and retrieving data. This issue comes and goes intermittently.
resolution:
Follow these steps to resolve the issue: 

1. Check the system logs for any relevant error messages related to the storage degradation issue. 
2. Verify that there are no issues with the hardware or software components of the storage array. 
3. Run a disk check on the affected volume to identify and repair any errors or corruption. 
4. If the above steps do not resolve the issue, consider contacting technical support for further assistance.

title: Storage array degraded due to disk failure
description: End-user is reporting that their storage array has become degraded and they are unable to access certain files. They have also reported that the volume capacity is low. The user is frustrated and needs assistance in resolving this issue as soon as possible.
resolution: 1. Check the logs for any error messages related to the disk failure. 2. Replace the failed disk with a new one. 3. Verify that the new disk is functioning properly. 4. Monitor the storage array for any further issues and replace any additional disks that may fail.

title: Sudden complete failure of NAS volume
description: The NAS (Network Attached Storage) device has experienced a sudden complete failure, resulting in the inability to access any files on the mounted volumes. The issue is believed to be related to the disk inside the NAS.
resolution: ['Check the logs of the NAS for any error messages that may indicate the cause of the failure.', 'Verify that all disks are functioning properly and have sufficient capacity to meet the demands of the NAS volume.', 'Check the NAS mount points on all client machines to ensure they are correctly configured and pointing to the correct IP address and port.', 'Replace the failed disk with a new one that is of adequate capacity to meet the needs of the NAS volume.', 'Perform a full system backup of the NAS before restoring any files from backups.', 'Test the restored files to ensure they are accessible and functional.']

title: NAS Mount Degraded and Delayed Access
description: End-user is reporting that their NAS mount is degraded and delayed in accessing files. They are unable to browse or search for specific files on the network.
resolution: 1. Check the network connectivity between the end-user's device and the NAS server. 2. Verify that the NAS service is running and available. 3. Ensure that there are no issues with the disk space or file permissions on the NAS. 4. Clear the cache on the end-user's device by unmounting and remounting the NAS drive. If the issue persists, contact the network administrator for further assistance.

title: Unstable NAS Mount Issue
description: User is experiencing an issue where their NAS mount is unstable and causing intermittent file access problems. The problem seems to be affecting a single user.
resolution: 1. Verify the capacity of the NAS and ensure it is not running at full capacity. 2. Check the network connection between the user's machine and the NAS server. 3. Restart both the user's machine and the NAS server. 4. If the problem persists, consider checking the mount points and permissions for the user.

title: Storage Alert - Disk Mount Issue
description: A monitoring alert has fired overnight indicating an issue with the disk mount at /mnt/data. The volume capacity is showing as full and the mount point is unresponsive.
resolution:
1. Check the status of the disk by running the command 'sudo fdisk -l'.
2. If the disk is marked as 'no' in the 'bootable' column, update the boot order to include the correct disk.
3. If the disk is still not responsive after changing the boot order, try remounting the volume using the command 'sudo mount /mnt/data'.
4. If the issue persists, perform a disk check by running the command 'sudo fsck -f /dev/sdaX' (replace 'X' with the partition number of the affected disk).
5. If the disk check fails, consider replacing the disk and updating the volume.

title: Storage issue with flapping nas mount
description: A monitoring alert was triggered overnight indicating that a nas mount had started flapping. Upon investigation, it was discovered that the capacity of the storage system has been exceeded due to an increase in file inodes. This is causing the system to become unresponsive and unable to mount the nas share. The system log shows several errors related to file I/O operations.
resolution:
To resolve this issue, please follow these steps: 

1. Review the usage of the storage system to identify any potential capacity issues. This may include reviewing usage reports or running capacity utilization tests. 
2. Free up space on the storage system by deleting unnecessary files or reducing the size of existing files. 
3. Once capacity has been freed up, run a file system repair operation to ensure that the system is stable and able to mount the nas share properly. This can be done using a disk utility tool such as fsck. 
4. Verify that the nas mount is functioning correctly by attempting to mount it again. If issues persist, please provide additional information or contact storage support for further assistance.

title: Recurring RAID Array Volume Capacity Issue
description: The RAID array volume capacity on the NAS mount is running low and causing recurring problems for users.
resolution:
1. Log in to the server console and identify the specific volume that is experiencing issues.
2. Check the current volume capacity and compare it to the total storage capacity of the RAID array.
3. If the volume is near full capacity, create a new volume on an adjacent free space within the RAID array to redistribute data.
4. Verify that the new volume has the same mount point as the original volume and is accessible by all affected users.
5. Monitor the performance of the RAID array and adjust the configuration as needed to ensure optimal performance.

title: Raid Array Disk LUN Failed for Single User
description: The RAID array containing the lun associated with user XYZ has failed, resulting in the user being unable to access their data. The issue is occurring intermittently and is causing significant performance issues.
resolution:
1. Verify that all components of the RAID array are functioning properly by running a thorough checkup.
2. If the checkup reveals any errors or inconsistencies, perform a full backup of the affected data to an external storage device.
3. Restore the backup data to a new lun on the remaining disks in the array, ensuring that the restored data is accessible to the user. Repeat step 1 to verify that all components are functioning properly.
4. If the issue persists, upgrade or replace the faulty disk(s) to prevent future failures.

title: NAS RAID Disk Volume Capacity Issue
description: The NAS RAID disk has reached its volume capacity and cannot be expanded.
resolution:
To resolve this issue, please follow these steps: 
1. Identify the affected volume on the NAS RAID array. 
2. Determine if additional disk space is available for expansion by reviewing the available storage capacity on each connected disk. 
3. If there is sufficient available space, add new disks to the RAID array using the appropriate configuration settings. 
4. If the RAID array does not support adding new disks or if no additional disk space is available, consider migrating data to another storage solution with increased capacity.

title: Recurring Disk Space Issues on RAID Volume
description: The RAID volume containing critical application data has been experiencing intermittent disk space issues over the past few weeks. This problem seems to occur at random intervals and resolves itself without any intervention. The affected point of failure is not consistently identifiable, making it difficult to troubleshoot.
resolution: 1. Analyze the disk usage report for the RAID volume to identify the specific files or folders causing the disk space issues. This information can help prioritize which data needs to be backed up and where it should be stored. 2. Review the RAID configuration to ensure that all disks are functioning properly and are not overloaded with too much data. If necessary, consider adding an additional disk or adjusting the RAID layout. 3. Configure a backup plan for critical application data to prevent any potential data loss. This may involve setting up redundant storage or implementing regular backups to offsite locations.

title: Mount Raid Array issue
description: User is experiencing intermittent issues with mounting a raid array. Error message: 'mount: error 192: Inode or directory for file system not found'. The problem seems to recur every few days.
resolution: 1. Verify that the raid array is configured correctly and that all disks are connected properly. 2. Check the file system of the raid array for any corruption by running a fsck command. 3. Ensure that the user has sufficient permissions to access the raid array. 4. If none of the above steps resolve the issue, consider reinstalling the operating system and restoring the data from backups.

title: Storage Volume Capacity Alert
description: An alert was triggered overnight indicating that the storage volume on server XYZ is at full capacity.
resolution:
Please free up some disk space on server XYZ to prevent further issues. Steps to take: 
1. Log in to server XYZ as an administrator
2. Open the Disk Management tool
3. Identify the storage volume that is full (drive letter may vary)
4. Right-click on the drive and select 'Properties'
5. In the Properties window, click on the 'Tools' tab
6. Select 'Check'
7. Follow the prompts to scan for errors and free up space as needed.

title: Storage issue with unstable performance and delayed data transfer
description: The storage system has been experiencing an ongoing problem of poor performance and delayed data transfer for several months. This has resulted in users experiencing delays while working on their files, which is impacting productivity.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Check the lun's capacity and ensure that it is not running out of space.
2. Review the storage array's configuration to ensure that it is optimized for performance.
3. Analyze the network connection and verify that there are no issues with latency or bandwidth limitations.
4. Update the storage drivers to the latest version and perform a reboot.
5. Contact the vendor for further support if the issue persists.

title: NAS mount unstable
description: User reports intermittent issues with NAS mount on their Windows machine. Mounting the NAS drive seems to come and go randomly.
resolution: 1. Verify that the NAS is powered on and accessible from other devices. 2. Check the network connection on the user's machine. Ensure that the Ethernet cable is securely connected and working properly. 3. If the network connection is stable, try to connect to the NAS using a different drive letter. 4. If the issue persists, reboot the NAS and the user's computer. If the problem still occurs after the reboot, please contact the vendor for further assistance.

title: Storage Disk Failure at Mount Point
description: A monitoring alert has been triggered overnight at point /mnt/data. The issue appears to be related to the lun attached to disk sdb1. Upon investigation, it was found that the disk has failed and is no longer responding.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Identify the failing disk (sdb1).
2. Verify that the lun is properly mounted at /mnt/data.
3. If necessary, unmount the failing lun using the command 'umount /mnt/data'.
4. Run a disk check on the failed disk using the command 'sudo smartctl --check' to identify any errors or bad sectors.
5. Once errors have been identified and corrected (if possible), create a new lun using the command 'sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1'.
6. Reattach the new lun to the mount point at /mnt/data.
7. Verify that the disk is now functioning properly by running another disk check (using step 4).
8. If necessary, update any affected applications or configurations to use the new mount point and disk path.

title: Storage Domain Flapping Incident
description: A sudden complete failure has occurred with the NAS storage. It appears that the LUN disk has flipped and is now causing a complete outage of the storage system. The error logs indicate that the disk has failed to mount properly, leading to an unavailable drive letter.
resolution: The following steps can be taken to resolve this issue: 1. Remove the flapping LUN from the storage array 2. Run a check on the NAS storage to ensure that all disks are functioning properly 3. If any disks are found to be bad, replace them with new ones 4. Mount the drives in a consistent manner 5. Once the drives are mounted and functioning properly, assign drive letters accordingly

title: Slow performance on user's computer due to full raid array volume capacity
description: The user's computer is experiencing slow performance and intermittent freezes. Upon investigation, it was found that the raid array has reached its maximum capacity, causing delays in accessing files.
resolution:
1. Backup all critical data from the affected raid array to an external hard drive or cloud storage.
2. Replace the affected raid array with a new one that has at least twice the volume capacity of the existing one.
3. Restore the backup data to the new raid array.

title: NAS Mount Issue with Volume Capacity
description: The NAS mount for the file server has stopped functioning after an update. Users are unable to access any files on the storage device and receive an error message indicating that the volume capacity is exceeded.
resolution: 1. Check the capacity of the storage device by running a disk space check command. This will help identify any files or directories that are taking up more space than they should be. 2. Use a disk cleanup tool to delete unnecessary files and free up space on the storage device. 3. Ensure that all hard drives are formatted properly and have enough available space to accommodate the current storage needs. 4. If the issue persists, consider upgrading the storage device or replacing the existing one with a larger capacity model.

title: Storage issue with intermittent mount point
description: The NAS mount at /mnt/nas has been experiencing intermittent issues where it comes and goes. This issue has been affecting access to the volume capacity.
resolution: 1. Verify that the network connection between the client and the storage device is stable. If not, troubleshoot the network connectivity by following standard networking best practices. 2. Check the disk status of the storage device to ensure it's functioning correctly. If the disk is failing, replace it with a new one. 3. Verify that the mount point is set up correctly and all permissions are configured properly. Run a file system check to ensure the integrity of the mounted volume. If the issue persists, consider using a different mount point.

title: Storage Array Issue with Mount Point and LUN
description: We are experiencing delayed performance issues with our storage array that is affecting the entire team and site. We believe the issue may be related to a problem with the mount point and lun.
resolution: Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 1. Check if the mount point for the affected lun is correct and pointing to the correct location on the storage array. 2. If the mount point is correct, check if the lun is mounted properly and if it has enough space available. 3. If the lun is mounted correctly, try unmounting and remounting it. 4. If the issue persists, contact the storage vendor for further assistance.

title: Storage Volume Capacity Issue
description: End-user reports that their NAS mount is showing low volume capacity.
resolution: Check the storage device's physical capacity and verify that it is not at maximum capacity. If the device is at full capacity, consider upgrading to a larger model or adding additional storage devices. Once the issue has been resolved, remount the NAS and check the volume capacity again.

title: Gradual Degradation of Storage Array
description: Over the past few days, there has been a gradual degradation in performance and capacity of our storage array. Users are reporting slow access times and intermittent errors when attempting to save or retrieve files. The array is set up in RAID configuration for high availability and redundancy, but it seems that one or more disks may be failing.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Perform a disk check on each individual disk within the array using the `chkdsk` command. This will scan for any errors or bad sectors and report back any issues. 
2. If any errors are found during the disk check, replace the affected disk with a new one. It is recommended to use a drive with the same capacity as the original disk to maintain consistency within the array. 
3. After replacing the disk, run another disk check to ensure that all disks are functioning properly. 
4. If the issue persists after completing these steps, it may be necessary to reconfigure the RAID array or consider upgrading to a newer, more efficient storage solution.

title: Intermittent NAS Mount Capacity Issue
description: The capacity of the disk on the NAS server seems to be fluctuating intermittently and causing issues with the nas mount. This problem comes and goes and is causing performance degradation for multiple applications running on the storage domain.
resolution: Check the disk usage using the command "df -h" to identify which disk is experiencing the issue. Once identified, use the command "fdisk /dev/sda1" to see the partition table for that disk and check if there are any corrupt or missing partitions. If there are any issues with the partition table, create a new partition using the command "mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdaX", where X is the number of the partition being created. If there are no issues with the partition table, run the command "fsck /dev/sda1" to repair any file system errors. After completing these steps, the NAS mount should be stable and the issue should be resolved.

title: Storage Array Issue with Volume Access
description: After updating the Storage Area Network (SAN) software, users are experiencing issues accessing their NAS volumes on the array. This issue started immediately after the update and has caused disruptions in file sharing and storage operations.
resolution:
1. Identify which NAS volume is causing the issue by logging into the SAN web interface. 
2. Check the SAN event logs for any errors or warnings related to the NAS volume. 
3. Verify that the NAS volume is mounted correctly on all client systems. 
4. Update the NAS software on each client system to the latest version. 
5. Test file sharing and storage operations to ensure the issue has been resolved.

title: Storage issue with NAS mount
description: The NAS mounted on user's computer is showing a full disk error message.
resolution:
1. Restart the NAS server
2. Check the hard drive space usage and delete unnecessary files to free up space
3. Unmount the affected volume from the user's computer and remount it after cleaning up space.

title: Storage Degradation - NAS Mount Issue
description: The company's network-attached storage (NAS) device has been experiencing a gradual degradation of capacity over the past few days. This issue is affecting users' ability to access files and folders stored on the NAS. The specific point of failure is the nas mount, which has become unresponsive. This has led to slow performance, frequent errors, and intermittent data loss. The impact on business operations has been significant.
resolution: The following steps are required to resolve this issue: 1) Perform a backup of all critical data stored on the NAS device. 2) Restart the NAS device and attempt to re-mount it. If successful, proceed to step 3. 3) If the nas mount is still unresponsive, perform a disk check on the relevant storage point. This will identify any corruption or damage that may be causing the issue. 4) Once the disk check has been completed, replace any faulty or damaged disks with new ones. 5) After replacing the disks, perform another backup of all critical data and attempt to re-mount the nas device. If successful, then the issue is resolved. If not, please provide an update on the incident status.

title: Storage Inode Mount Issue
description: User reports intermittent issues where a specific disk mount on a server is showing full and the mount point folder cannot be accessed. This issue only happens sporadically and does not occur consistently.
resolution: Check the file system usage and disk space of the affected disk to determine if there is an issue with the inode count. Verify that the disk has enough free space and that no process or application is holding onto the disk's resources. If the issue persists, check for any pending disk operations or file transfers that may be causing delays or blocking issues. After identifying the cause, consider resizing the disk, reinstalling the affected software, or implementing a file system optimization tool to improve performance and free up space.

title: Storage Device Failed and Filling Up
description: A storage device has failed and is causing issues with the NAS server. Full LUNs are also impacting performance on the site. This is affecting the entire team.

title: Storage System Disk Space Issue with NAS
description: A user has reported an issue with a storage system running a Network Attached Storage (NAS) device. They have noticed that disk space is rapidly being consumed and the system is becoming unresponsive. The issue started right after a recent update to the operating system of the NAS.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Open the terminal window on the NAS device. 
2. Identify the affected Logical Volume Unit (LUN) by checking its inode number using the following command: "lsblk | grep [lun_name]". Replace [lun_name] with the name of the LUN you want to check. 
3. Check the status of the RAID array that contains the LUN by running the following command: "mdadm detail [raid_array_name]". Replace [raid_array_name] with the name of the RAID array. 
4. If the RAID array is not in a healthy state, follow the instructions provided by the mdadm manual to repair it. Once the RAID array is repaired, try to rebuild the LUN using the following command: "mkfs.ext[file_system_version] [lun_name]". Replace [file_system_version] with the version of the file system used by the LUN. 
5. Once the LUN is rebuilt, try to mount it again using the following command: "mount -t [file_system_type] [lun_name] /mnt/[mount_point]". Replace [file_system_type] with the type of file system used by the LUN and [mount_point] with the desired mount point. 
6. If the issue persists, contact the vendor for further assistance.

4. If the issue persists, contact your vendor for further assistance. They may recommend updates or configuration changes to improve performance and stability.

title: Storage Volume Flapping Issue
description: The storage volume attached to LUN 1234 is flapping and not mounting properly on the server.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 

1. Check the status of the network interface on the server where the volume is mounted. If it's down, restart the network adapter.

2. Verify that the LUN is available and accessible by checking its status on the storage array console. If the LUN is offline or not ready, wait for it to come online before proceeding.

3. Attempt to mount the volume again using the following command: `mount /dev/sdb1234 /mnt/volume_name` (replace sdb1234 with the appropriate device name and volume_name with the desired name for the mounted volume). If the volume fails to mount, it may be due to incorrect permissions or ownership. In this case, check the file system ACLs and adjust them as needed.

4. If the issue persists, try restarting the storage array to reset any configuration issues that may be causing the problem.

title: Storage Domain: Mount Volume Capacity Check and Inode Count Adjustment
description: Intermittent issues are reported with the storage volume capacity check. The problematic volume is mounted on a server that runs critical applications. The issue causes delays in application processing times and affects overall system performance. Additionally, the volume's inode count has increased significantly over time, causing potential data loss and system stability issues. It is recommended to check the volume capacity and adjust the inode count to maintain optimal performance.
resolution:
The following steps should be taken to resolve the issue: 
1. Check the storage volume capacity using the command "df -h" on the server where the problematic volume is mounted. If the volume capacity is approaching or at full, consider deleting unnecessary files from the volume or increasing the volume's size if possible.
2. Adjust the inode count for the problematic volume using the command "fsck -f -r /dev/sdX". Replace "/dev/sdX" with the path to the problematic volume. This will force a file system check and rebuild of the volume, which may result in some data loss. If data loss is not acceptable, it is recommended to take a backup before performing this step. After the fsck command completes, the inode count for the volume should be checked again using the command "df -h".

title: Storage issue with NAS mount

resolution:

1. Stop the flapping NAS mount using the following command:
```sudo systemctl stop nas-server.service```
2. Check the disk '/mnt/nas/johndoe' for errors and repair any bad sectors if necessary.
3. Mount the NAS drive again using the following command:
```sudo mount -t cifs //IP_ADDRESS/nas /mnt/nas```
4. Verify that the NAS server is reachable and accessible by the user 'johndoe'. If not, please open a new ticket for further investigation.

title: Storage RAID LUN I/O Delayed
description: An alert has been generated in the Storage monitoring system indicating that there is a delay in I/O operations on a specific RAID LUN.
resolution:

resolution:

2. Free up space on the disk by deleting unnecessary files or optimizing the disk using a tool like 'sudo du -h /dev/sdb1' and following the recommendations provided.

title: Storage Array Failure
description: The storage array has failed suddenly and completely. Volume mounted on /mnt/data is unavailable.
resolution:
Check the logs of the storage array for any error messages indicating a possible cause of the failure. Once identified, perform the following steps to recover data: 
1. Identify the affected disk within the storage array by reviewing the array's configuration. 
2. Unmount the volume using the command 'umount /mnt/data'. 
3. Use the command 'grep' to locate the corresponding mount point for the affected disk in the directory hierarchy. 
4. Remove the mount point using the command 'rm' (with the '-rf' option to force removal). 
5. Check if the disk is marked as read-only, and if so, change it back to read-write using the command 'mount -o remount /dev/sdb1'. 
6. Mount the disk again by running the command 'mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/data'. If the volume still does not mount successfully, consider performing a disk check or creating a new file system.

title: Storage Alert: Lun Filled Up
description: A monitoring alert has been triggered overnight indicating that the lun with mount point /mnt/lunX has reached 100% capacity and is now full. This is causing issues with accessing data stored on this lun.
resolution:
To resolve this issue, please follow these steps: 
1. Log in to the storage system as an administrator. 
2. Use the command 'lsblk' to identify the name of the lun that is full. For example, if the mount point is /mnt/lunX, the name of the lun may be '/dev/sdbX'. 
3. Use the command 'df -h' to verify the capacity of the lun and confirm that it has reached 100%. 
4. Determine the maximum capacity of the lun by running the command 'lsblk /dev/sdbX | grep Size' (this will give you the size in bytes). 
5. Use the command 'resize2fs -f -r /dev/sdbX +<amount_to_add_space>' to increase the capacity of the lun by the desired amount. For example, if the maximum capacity is 1TB and the current capacity is 90GB, you can use the command 'resize2fs -f -r /dev/sdbX +10g'. 
6. After increasing the capacity of the lun, run the command 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdbX' to format the new space. 
7. Use the command 'mount /dev/sdbX /mnt/lunX' to mount the lun on the original mount point.

resolution:

2. Run a disk check on the affected volume by executing the command "sudo fsck /dev/sdbX", where X is the partition letter of the affected volume.

3. Once the disk check is complete, resize the volume to increase its capacity by executing the command "sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/sdbX bs=1M count=2G". Replace X with the partition letter of the affected volume.

4. After the volume has been resized, remount it by executing the command "mount /dev/sdbX /path/to/volume".

5. Finally, run a disk check on the newly formatted volume to ensure that all inodes are functioning properly by executing the command "sudo fsck /dev/sdbX". If any errors are found, repeat steps 2-4 until the issue is resolved.

resolution: 1. Shut down the NAS server. 2. Check the RAID array for any failed drives. 3. Replace the failed drives if necessary. 4. Reformat the RAID array. 5. Mount the NAS server again.

title: Unstable Storage Mount Issue
description: The mount point for LUN [insert LUN number here] is experiencing intermittent stability issues.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 

1. Verify that the LUN is properly configured and available. Check the VAAI status of the LUN to see if it's marked as unavailable. If it is, work with your storage administrator to resolve any issues related to the LUN. 

2. Try mounting the LUN manually by using the following command: `mount /dev/sdbX /mnt/lun`. Replace X with the appropriate letter for your system's block device mapping. If this is successful, the issue may be related to a problem with the file system on the mount point. 

3. If the manual mount was successful, remount the LUN automatically by editing the fstab file and adding the following line: `/dev/sdbX /mnt/lun auto,noatime`. Save and reboot the server. 

4. If the issue persists, check for any updates or patches related to the storage or file system drivers that may be necessary. Apply any available patches and reboot the server. 

5. If the issue continues after following all of these steps, please work with your storage administrator to investigate further.

title: Unstable NAS Mount - Disk Error
description: User is experiencing an unstable mount on their NAS server which has been affecting their ability to access files on the disk.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 

1. Check if any disk errors exist by running a disk check utility. If there are any errors, please correct them before proceeding.
2. Verify that the NAS server has enough available disk space. If necessary, free up some space by deleting unnecessary files or folders from the disk.
3. Restart the NAS server and wait for it to fully restart. This may take several minutes depending on the size of the NAS. After the restart, try accessing the file system again.

title: Storage Issue - Volume Capacity Exceeded
description: User X has reported that their volume capacity has been exceeded on LUN Y. This issue is causing the user's access to the affected files and folders to be unavailable.
resolution:
1. Identify the volume capacity of the affected LUN using the command 'df -h'.
2. Determine the location of the affected file(s) or folder(s).
3. Manually delete or move the affected file(s) or folder(s) to a different location with sufficient available space.
4. Update the volume capacity of the affected LUN using the command 'fsck -f' followed by 'ext4 fs -L <lun-name>'.
5. Verify that the issue has been resolved by checking the user's access to the affected files and folders.

The mounted file system cannot be accessed and no data can be retrieved from the affected drive.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Verify that the update did not cause any data loss by checking the backups of the affected drives. If there are no backups, data recovery may not be possible.
2. Check the disk space usage on the affected drive and ensure that there is enough free space available. You can use the df command to check the disk space usage. If the disk is full, you may need to delete some files or increase the size of the drive. 
3. Unmount the failed RAID volume using the umount command. For example: "umount /mnt/raid1". 
4. Create a new RAID set on the affected drives using the mdadm command. For example: "mdadm --create /dev/sda1,/dev/sdb1,/dev/sdc1 md0" (replace sda1, sdb1 and sdc1 with the appropriate device names). 
5. Format the new RAID set using the mkfs.ext4 command. For example: "mkfs.ext4 /dev/md0" (replace md0 with the name of the new RAID set). 
6. Mount the new RAID volume using the mount command. For example: "mount /dev/md0 /mnt/raid1". If the mount fails, please check the file system for any errors or inconsistencies using the fsck command.

description: A storage array is causing issues with the mount point of a drive on Windows Server 2016. The issue seems to be intermittent and comes and goes. resolution:

1. Open Device Manager on the affected machine and navigate to the device for the storage array in question. Right-click the device and select 'Properties.'

title: Storage Issue with Volume Capacity on RAID Inode Mount
description: After updating the server, a storage issue has occurred on one of the mounted volumes in RAID configuration. The volume is showing up as low capacity despite having enough free space according to the file system.
resolution:
The issue is likely caused by an incorrect calculation of free space on the RAID array due to corruption of the inode metadata. Here are the steps to resolve the issue: 

1. Unmount the affected volume using the following command: "umount /mnt/raid1"
2. Check for any corrupted inodes using the fsck utility on the RAID array: "fsck -v -y /dev/sda1"
3. If any corrupted inodes are found, run the fsck utility again with the -r flag to repair the metadata: "fsck -v -y /dev/sda1 -r"
4. Once the fsck command has completed, remount the volume using the following command: "mount /mnt/raid1"
5. Finally, run a disk usage check to confirm that the volume capacity is now being reported correctly: "df -h"

title: Storage array volume capacity issue
description: A monitoring alert was triggered overnight for a storage array mounted at /mnt/data with an array configuration of RAID-5. The volume capacity is now showing as full and the array is unresponsive.
resolution:
Please follow these steps to resolve the issue: 
1. Verify that there are no pending operations on the array using the `dmesg | grep sdaX` command where X represents the array device name. If there are any, wait for them to complete before proceeding. 
2. Mount the array again with a read-only option by executing the following command: `mount -o remount /mnt/data` 
3. Create a new array volume by executing the following command: `mdadm --detail | grep Array: | awk '{print $5}' | xargs sudo mdadm create --array=<Array Name> --chunk=64M <Volume Name>`. Replace <Array Name> with the name of your RAID array and <Volume Name> with a unique name for the new volume. 
4. Unmount the old volume by executing the following command: `umount /mnt/data` 
5. Mount the new volume to the same mount point as before by executing the following command: `mount -o remount /mnt/data`. If you encounter any errors during this process, please provide the error message and we will investigate further. After completing these steps, the array should be responsive again and the volume capacity should be available.

description: The storage volume for the RAID 5 array has been unstable and showing a decrease in free space since a recent update to the operating system. resolution:

4. If the file system is in good condition, create a new RAID 5 configuration on the storage device using the command 'mdadm --detail --create /dev/sdb1 --chunksize=64M --raid-algorithm=linear --metadata=ext3 --name=storage'. 
5. Mount the new file system to the server at the path /mnt/storage.
6. Verify that the new RAID 5 configuration is working properly by checking the free space on the storage device using the command 'df -h /mnt/storage'.

title: Storage Volume is Full
